difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own theorem realcompleteness at source lines 944-946: the set of cuts, ordered by inclusion, has the least-upper-bound property. The proof at source lines 948-968 is the classical Dedekind construction and is not a routine application of a stated completeness axiom in the unit. It starts from an arbitrary non-empty set S of cuts with an upper bound, forms the union lambda, and then has to verify the three clauses of the definition of a cut one by one: that lambda is non-empty and strictly smaller than the rationals (which uses both hypotheses, and where the strictness needs the upper bound to supply a rational absent from every member of S), that lambda is downward closed under the order on rationals, and that lambda has no greatest element. Only after that does it prove the two upper-bound clauses, first that lambda contains every member of S, then that any other upper bound contains lambda, again by an element-wise argument. The order in which the hypotheses are used is not visible in the statement. No result outside the retained text is used.
